title: Metric entropy day-zero kit: operator onboarding and dashboard hygiene
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operator-focused "day-zero" kit to tame metric entropy for inference services. The doc is practical: metric naming guardrails, initial tracing annotation patterns, a lightweight dashboard-pruning checklist, and a short experiment plan for bursty token workloads. This is intentionally opinionated to help new operators make safe, repeatable decisions in the first week after joining a model rollout or incident rotation.

Audience and scope:
- Primary: oncall engineers, observability stewards, SREs supporting inference runtime and routing layers.
- Scope: runtime+serving stacks (request fanout, kv-cache, batching), model routing, and UI dashboards used by ops. Not a full instrumentation design — this is the minimal practical kit.

Quick glossary (short):
- Metric entropy: total count of unique TS keys+label cardinality inflating query and storage cost.
- Micro-SLI: concise SLI tied to an operator action (e.g., P95 TTF token, cold-cache-rate).
- Session context: trace/span annotations that correlate request-level metadata (tenant, route, model_variant, kv_hit).

Principles / guardrails (high level):
1) Name once, reuse everywhere. Metric names should be stable; avoid per-tenant/name variants in the name. Favor tags/labels for variable dimensions with strict allowed values.
2) Protect cardinality. Only label on dimensions that will be queried. Limit free-form labels (e.g., prompt_hash) to hashed + sampled trace attributes, not metrics.
3) SLI-first: define 3 operational SLIs per service (latency, error, cache_warmth). Dashboards should start from SLIs, not the other way around.
4) Cost-awareness: run a weekly audit of metric ingestion and trace volume; prune unused counters older than 4 weeks.

Suggested metric definitions (minimal set) — names + short semantics:
- inference.requests.total : counter, increment per request ingress. Labels: service, route, model_variant, priority (low|normal|high)
- inference.tokens.generated : counter, total tokens emitted per request. Labels: service, model_variant
- inference.latency.p50/p95/p99 : histogram/summary for end-to-end latency (ms). Labels: service, route, model_variant
- inference.kvcache.hit_rate : gauge (0..1) sampled per minute. Labels: service, model_variant, cache_tier (local|shared)
- inference.cold_cache_fraction : gauge, fraction of requests that experienced a cold K/V miss on first token. Labels: service, route
- inference.batch.size.histogram : histogram of batch sizes observed (buckets tuned to 1,2,4,8,16,32+, labels: service, queue_type)
- inference.routing.fallback.rate : counter or rate of requests that routed to fallback model_variant. Labels: service, route, reason
- inference.errors.by_class : counter broken down by class (timeout|oom|parse_error|model_error). Labels: service, model_variant

Label hygiene rules (short):
- Allowed label cardinalities: service(~10), route(~100), model_variant(~20), cache_tier(2), priority(3).
- Block free-text labels: prompt_type, user_message. If needed, capture hashed prompt fingerprints in traces only and sample to <1% of requests.

Tracing annotations (practical spec):
- Core spans: request:ingress, request:router, model:dispatch, model:inference, kvcache:lookup, kvcache:hydrate, response:serialize
- Mandatory span tags: tenant_id (hashed), route, model_variant, request_id, agent_version, sequence_length, kv_hit (true|false)
- Sample policy: deterministic 100% lightweight sampling for headers/ids only (no payload); detailed spans (with prompt fingerprint) sampled at 0.5% globally; increase to 2% for canary routes.
- Trace size guardrails: max_span_payload_size = 2KB; truncate any prompt/payload fields beyond that in the tracer.

Dashboard pruning checklist (operator day-zero):
- Run through every panel in the runtime dashboard and mark: SLI / Helpful / Nice-to-have / Candidate-delete. Aim to delete 25% of panels initially.
- For each panel, verify there is an owning team and an investigation playbook — otherwise mark for archive.
- Replace high-cardinality live tables with sampled summaries (top-k tenants) and a drilldown query instead of wide joins.
- Add a compact incident surface: 4 widgets that show (1) P95 latency by route, (2) cold_cache_fraction, (3) active queue depth, (4) recent routing fallbacks. Keep this visible on the primary ops screen.

Probe scheduling & burst mitigation notes:
- Bursty token workloads cause ephemeral metric spikes and trace surges. Schedule synthetic probes with the same token-length distribution as traffic (not single short probes). Run probes staggered across model_variant and region to avoid correlated bursts.
- Probe cadence: default 1 probe every 10s per probe-shard; increase to 1/5s when measuring warm-up profiles. Probe budget should not exceed 0.1% of production tokens.

Short experiment plan (week-1):
1) Baseline: enable the minimal metric set and 0.5% trace sampling. Run 7 days to collect baseline storage and dashboard costs.
2) Prune pass: identify top-20 metrics by ingestion cost and remove/aggregate 10 of them.
3) Sampling ramp: test reducing trace detail across low-priority routes and confirm no loss in incident triage quality.
4) Dashboard consolidation: merge panels that are >90% correlated and introduce a micro-SLI screen.

Operator playbook snippets (quick):
- If P95 latency spikes but cold_cache_fraction is stable: suspect batching/backpressure — check worker queue depth and batch.size histogram.
- If cold_cache_fraction rises with no config change: look at kvcache:hydrate latency and eviction rate on shared caches.
- If fallback.rate increases: capture recent traces for route/model_variant and check slow model kernel selection or OOMs.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Do we want a soft quota for new metric registrations via a self-serve portal? (prevents accidental high-cardinality labels)
- Can the tracer enforce payload truncation and automatic prompt fingerprinting centrally?
- Confirm which SLIs live in product-facing dashboards vs ops-only; propose a separation policy.

Notes to self / action items:
- Asha: prototype ingestion-cost exporter for the top-200 metrics by bytes (JIRA-OBS-1427).
- Marcus: add kvcache.hit_rate to the canary probe harness and run in eu-west-1 for 48h.
- Priya: run dashboard prune session with owner roster and publish archived panels list.

References and bookmarks:
- Confluence: metric-onboarding-playbook (linked above)
- GitHub PR for trace truncation: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/812
- Jira: JIRA-OBS-1427

Quick closing: this is intentionally compact — the goal is repeatability for new operators. If an oncall rotation can follow the Baseline → Prune → Sampling steps above in the first sprint, the observable surface will be far more actionable and cheaper to operate.
